children: Mortgage Bankers Association's Composite Index decreased 1.5% to 227.3 during the week ended September 18, compared to -4.1% to 230.8 seen in the prior week, according to the Weekly Mortgage Applications Survey.
The Market Composite Index is a measure of mortgage loan application volume.
The Purchase Index dropped 0.8% to 154.9 vs. -0.8% to 156.2 a week ago, while the Refinance Index fell 2.6% to 611.0 vs. -8.8% to 627.1 in the previous period.
30-year fixed-rate mortgages rose to 7.12% from 6.97%, the highest level since May 2024.

"With fixed rates much higher, more borrowers opted for ARMs, with the ARM share reaching 9.8%, as rates for 5/1 ARMs were more than a percentage point lower than those for fixed rate loans," said Mike Fratantoni, MBA's senior vice president and chief economist.

"Applications for both refinance and purchase loans declined further last week, noting that the comparison is to the week that included the Labor Day holiday. With this week's decline, the pace of refinancing fell to its slowest pace since February 2025," said Fratantoni.

title: Mortgage demand drops as rates cross 7% mark
